payload.rationale: Precast concrete piles are required directly for the Piling activity, which starts shortly after the delivery date.
Rebar and mesh delivered 2026-12-02 directly supports pile caps and ground beams construction starting 2026-12-07.
Roof membrane and insulation boards are required for the roof covering and waterproofing activity starting shortly after the delivery date.
Plasterboard and metal studs are directly required for drylining and partitions, which starts shortly after the planned delivery date.
Block paving and landscaping materials are directly required for the External works and landscaping activity starting shortly after delivery.
Sanitaryware delivery on 2027-06-16 directly precedes and supplies the kitchen and bathroom fit-out activity starting 2027-06-21.
LVT floor finishes are installed during the decoration and flooring activity, with delivery shortly before its start date.
The structural steel frame delivery on 2026-12-29 directly precedes and supplies the steel frame erection activity A05 starting 2027-01-04.
Composite metal decking is directly required for activity A06, Metal decking and upper floor slabs L1-L5, which starts shortly after the planned delivery.
Unitised curtain wall panels are delivered just before the curtain walling and cladding activity begins installation.
Aluminium double glazed windows are directly required for window installation, which starts shortly after the planned delivery date.
First fix pipework, cable and containment is directly required for the MEP first fix activity starting shortly after delivery.
The 13-person passenger lifts are delivered just before Lift installation (A14) starts, matching the typical lead-in for lift equipment to site.
Kitchen sets must be on site shortly before kitchen and bathroom fit-out begins on 2027-06-21.

options.title: Fast-track the envelope by overlapping curtain walling with the steel/decking sequence
options.rationale: A09 Curtain walling and cladding is critical and currently waits for all of A06 Metal decking and upper floor slabs to finish. The playbook allows facade installation to follow the frame floor by floor, so curtain walling can start once the lower floors are structurally ready rather than waiting for the top floor slab. This overlaps two currently sequential critical activities and shortens the chain into watertight.
options.risks: Needs the structural engineer and temporary works coordinator to confirm each floor is loaded and braced before cladding starts on it, and edge protection must be in place for curtain wall installers working above live decking operations - a genuine CDM 2015 interface risk if not sequenced carefully floor by floor. Requires tight coordination between the steel erector and Clearview Glazing Systems' installation gangs sharing the same crane and access.
options.cost: Mainly coordination and possibly additional temporary edge protection/mast climbers to allow both trades on site together; limited direct cost, say £5-10k for extra temporary works, assuming no extra crane shift is needed.

options.title: Crash decking and MEP first fix with extra gangs and shifts
options.rationale: Both A06 Metal decking and upper floor slabs and A12 MEP first fix are labour-driven critical activities with no material constraint once decking and first-fix materials are on site, and both sit on the critical path. Adding a second gang or running longer shifts on each can claw back days without touching the delivery or the sequence, within the playbook's 30% crashing guidance.
options.risks: Diminishing returns and quality risk from rushed decking welds/bolting and from first-fix services not being properly coordinated before drylining; requires overtime or weekend working consent from the local authority and confirmation that the site can safely host extra operatives at height and in confined service risers. Should be checked against float on A07/A08/A10 before committing, as pulling A06 forward could shift what is currently non-critical onto the critical path.
options.cost: Roughly two extra gangs across the two packages plus weekend/evening premiums, in the order of £20-30k, with the usual productivity loss from overtime working.

options.title: Expedite the steel delivery with Pennine Steel (supply-side recovery)
options.rationale: A05 Structural steel frame erection is the first critical activity hit by the late PO-24110 delivery, and every downstream critical activity (A06 decking, A09 curtain walling, A11 watertight, A12-A13-A16-A17, A19, A20) is pushed by the same amount. Pulling the steel delivery back towards the original 2026-12-29 date attacks the problem at its source rather than compressing work later in the programme, and avoids disturbing the planned sequence.
options.risks: Pennine Steel's mill rolling and fabrication slots are long-lead and hard to move at short notice; galvanising capacity may not flex. If they can only offer a partial pull-forward (e.g. first grid lines), full recovery won't be achieved. Any informal promise should be confirmed in writing before relying on it in the programme, and keep the delay correspondence for a possible claim against the supplier.
options.cost: Likely an expediting fee or priority charge from Pennine Steel, typically a few thousand pounds; no extra site labour cost if the date simply moves back.
